subject: MAP readout: performance evaluation results, repro gaps, and closure checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP readout: performance evaluation results, repro gaps, and closure checklist

Emma —

Thanks for taking the time this morning. Per our MAP (attached v1.3) I wanted to land the core artifacts from the benchmark run we discussed and call out the three items blocking a clean close:

- Results: attached CSV has the per-region TTFT/latency/throughput breakdown (summary below). We ran with your dataset subset (conv-100) and Redwood's standard inference profile (gptx-16k, batch size 8, kv_cache enabled).
  - 99P latency (TTFT start-to-first-token): 420ms
  - Median token latency: 12.4ms/token
  - Sustained throughput at 8 concurrent sessions: ~520 tokens/s
  - CPU-bound tails observed at high concurrency (spikes at 80–120ms)

- Methodology discrepancy: your infra team's load generator (Locust-based) produced ~15% lower latency than our internal runner for identical request traces. We captured traces in trace_samples_05-20.zip.

- Reproduction gap: Jorge noted higher TTFT in your dedicated region during yesterday's test. We could not reproduce that on Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2; the attached loadgen_config.diff highlights the slight differences in connection pacing and keepalive.

Next steps we propose (from MAP & close checklist):
1) Rishi to share a concise repro playbook (configs + command lines) and a deterministic trace file you can run locally.
2) Jorge to run the exact playbook in your staging region and upload logs to the Drive link.
3) Connor to validate kernel-level metrics and confirm whether quantization profiles diverge across hosts.
4) Marissa to update MAP with acceptance criteria and close date (target: 2026-05-28).

Please review the short readout and let me know if you want a focused engineering sync (30 min) this week to walk the repro steps.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Emma Li <emma.li@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jorge Ramires <jorge.ramirez@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP readout: performance evaluation results, repro gaps, and closure checklist

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear summary. Jorge and I dug into the traces this morning. A couple quick notes:

- We did not explicitly disable HTTP keepalive in our Locust config for the earlier runs; that could explain some of the lower latency numbers we saw.
- Our staging region uses a different NAT gateway config which changes ephemeral port reuse; we'll re-run with the keepalive off and push logs to the shared Drive link by EOD.

Can we aim for a short sync on Friday (May 22) at 10am PT so engineering teams can align? Jorge will bring the staging logs and I will attach our Locust runner command lines.

On acceptance: we are comfortable proceeding if TTFT 99P <= 450ms in your dedicated profile and throughput meets the MAP target of 480 tokens/s at 8 concurrent sessions.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li | Staff PM, Platform & AI — Acme Corp
emma.li@acme.com | +1 (202) 555-0109

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP readout: performance evaluation results, repro gaps, and closure checklist

Emma / team —

Thanks for the head's up. Quick technical notes from our triage (so the MAP reflects the right acceptance criteria and repro steps):

1) TTFT definition alignment
   - Your team used "time from SDK send() to first token received" measured inside a VM that includes local TCP dial time to the NAT. Our internal metric measures from Redwood edge (request accepted by LB) to first token emitted. That difference explains ~50–70ms variance and needs to be aligned for the MAP. Recommendation: run with the provided "edge-timestamped" trace we attached; that lets both sides compare the same stopwatch.

2) Load generator differences
   - Locust's default connection churn differs from our loadgen. We included loadgen_config.diff showing keepalive and concurrency ramp. For high-concurrency tails we also capture kernel-level contention (ephemeral ports, socket backlog) — Connor will share the kernel metric expectations.

3) Competitive comparison note (for your procurement stakeholders)
   - We ran a short run against a vendor X public endpoint using the same traces; vendor X showed similar median latency but had much higher variance at 8+ concurrency. We will include the summary in the MAP appendix but not in the headline acceptance criteria.

Action items:
- Rishi: push an "edge-timestamped" trace + deterministic runner by end of day (attached as perf_results_20260520.csv and trace samples).
- Jorge: run runner in staging and upload full logs to the Drive link.
- Connor: capture kernel counters (TIME_WAIT, socket backlog) during the next run and share a short screenshot.

I'll join Friday's 10am PT sync to go through the metrics if helpful.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0260

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP readout: performance evaluation results, repro gaps, and closure checklist

Emma / Jorge —

Thanks for running the staging tests and for the focused sync yesterday. Summary & closure path for the MAP:

- Repro status: Acme staging run (trace run id: acme-stg-0527-01) matched Redwood's edge-timestamped run within 5% for median latency and 7% for 99P after we disabled keepalive and used the provided runner. Good alignment.
- Outstanding: a small socket-timeout pattern in one of your hosts (host-12) — Connor confirmed this is likely due to ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT. Jorge will rotate the NAT gateway and re-run a short smoke test.
- Acceptance: per the MAP, Acme confirms the TTFT 99P target (<=450ms) and throughput target (>=480 tokens/s at 8 concurrent sessions).

Attachments updated in the MAP folder: redwood_map_v1.3.docx (MAP with acceptance criteria), perf_results_20260520.csv (edge-timestamped run), loadgen_config.diff, trace_samples_05-20.zip.

Next steps to close: Jorge to confirm NAT rotation & re-run smoke test (target: 2026-05-31). If successful, Marissa will mark the MAP as complete and issue the final close note and contract addendum.

If there's no objection, I'll prepare the final acceptance paragraph for signatures and a short one-pager for procurement.

Best,
Marissa
